The captioned appeal is filed by
the injured/claimant who is a minor girl questioning quantum and negligence in
MVC.No.940/2012.
In this case, appellant is aggrieved by the global compensation of Rs.25,000/- awarded towards injuries and the sum of Rs.12,198/- awarded towards medical expenses.
The Tribunal in all awarded a sum of Rs.37,198/- rounded off to Rs.37,200/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

3. The Tribunal in the absence of material evidence to demonstrate the permanent disability suffered, under Schedule II of M.V. Act, has awarded global compensation of 25,000/- and medical expenses of Rs.6,000/- in all Rs. 31,000/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Tribunal while attributing negligence held that the driver of the goods vehicle in which the claimant was traveling was negligent to the tune of 70% and the driver of the parked goods vehicle was negligent to the tune of 30%.

2 4.

The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to NC: 2024:KHC-K:9815 pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company Limited.
5.
Hence, the present appeal questioning both quantum as well as negligence.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.

FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:
7.

This Court in MFA.No.202567/2019 considering the arguments advanced by the counsel appearing for the claimants and the counsel appearing for both the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9815 Insurance Companies has after meticulous examination of the material on record and on an elaborate discussion held that both the drivers of the truck were negligent and therefore, attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
Accordingly, negligence is attributed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

Further more, since the truck bearing No. MH- 13-AX-2339 was used in violation of the policy conditions permitting 30 passengers to travel in the goods vehicle, Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the truck bearing No. MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.
FINDING ON QUANTUM:
8. This Court has independently reviewed the documents produced by the claimant.

In absence of NC: 2024:KHC-K:9815 medical evidence, Tribunal has proceeded to consider the quantum of compensation as mentioned in Schedule II of M.V. Act and has globally awarded Rs.25,000/- and Rs.6,000/- towards medical expenses.
9. There is no medical evidence indicating that appellant has suffered fractures which would warrant interference under the other heads.
Compensation of Rs.31,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is in accordance with law and does not warrant any enhancement.

10. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
